---
title: "Core concepts"
guide-section: "Understanding replaylab"
---

The vocabulary used everywhere else in the code and tests. Every term below
is explained on its own; the API Reference has the exact signatures.

# The game

**pool**
: The designs of one game — one target, one split. What an agent may buy from.

**game / campaign**
: A *game* is the static configuration (target, split, rounds, batch size,
  budget, delay — [`GameConfig`](../reference/config.GameConfig.qmd)); a
  *campaign* is one play of it against the
  [`CampaignStore`](../reference/store.CampaignStore.qmd).

**alias**
: Agents never see real design ids, only `d0001`-style aliases. The mapping is
  built by sorting real ids on `sha256(f"{seed}|{id}")` — identical on every
  machine, and **reshuffled by every seed** (a subtlety that has already bitten
  once: a similarity index keyed by the wrong seed's aliases silently scores
  the wrong sequences).

**round, tick, clock**
: Rounds are *batch slots*. `state.clock` counts elapsed rounds. `submit`
  creates a batch, hands it to the backend, ingests what is ready, then ticks
  once. A batch submitted at clock *t* with delay *d* delivers at *t + d* — so
  a delay of 1 looks identical to 0 to the agent, and `wait` (tick without
  buying) is allowed only while something is pending.

**batch**
: Designs proposed or submitted together, moving only forward through
  `proposed → submitted → partial → complete`.

# Status of a design

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **purchased** | in a batch that left `proposed` (delivered *or* pending); purchase order = batch order, then position inside the batch |
| **delivered** | its outcome has arrived and is in the store |
| **pending** | purchased but the outcome has not arrived yet |
| **unpurchased** | still available to buy |

# Outcomes

**hit**
: any binding record for the (design, target) pair is True. An *inconclusive*
  result (`hit is None`) is a purchase but **not** a hit, and is excluded from
  model fitting.

**conflict / strength / kd_molar**
: conflicting binding records; the strongest label (Strong/Medium/Weak); the
  smallest KD converted to molar units.

**budget**
: `rounds × batch_size` — every game spends at most its budget, and at most
  one round slot per submit.

# The agent side

**snapshot** ([`CampaignState`](../reference/domain.CampaignState.qmd))
: The immutable view a policy or advisor function receives: designs, batches,
  delivered outcomes, clock, and derived views (`unpurchased_ids`,
  `budget_remaining`, …). Everything the agent knows comes through this object.

**feature orientation**
: Feature values stay *raw* in the pool (a lower-is-better ProteinMPNN score
  looks lower); the ±1 orientation is applied once inside
  [`Preprocessor`](../reference/advisor.preprocess.Preprocessor.qmd), so every
  covariate points the same way before the model sees it.

**policy**
: `choose(state, k, rng) -> ids`. Returns `[]` to mean *stop*. The scripted
  ladder: `random`, `fixed:<metric>`, `learner`, `learner_sim`, each optionally
  wrapped in `WithStop`.

**stop rules**
: Advice evaluated at round boundaries on delivered purchases only.
  `low_yield` (the default): fires from 20 purchases when the cumulative hit
  rate is below 0.03. `decay` exists but was dropped from the default after it
  false-stopped 77–98% of runs; treat it as experimental.

**frozen configuration**
: `config/frozen_v1.yaml` pins the model hyper-parameters chosen on `N-dev`
  only. It changes only deliberately, never as a side effect of other work.

# Splits and evaluation

**dev / held-out split**
: Nipah-G designs are grouped into folds by sequence cluster (fold 2 is
  held out). The held-out outcomes can only be read with `final_run=True`, and
  the ladder refuses held-out games entirely — that split is run **once, at
  the end**.

**replay vs live**
: `mode="replay"` plays recorded outcomes through the
  [`ReplayBackend`](../reference/backends.ReplayBackend.qmd); `mode="live"`
  will drive a real campaign through the pinned OpenAPI spec.
  Both implement the same three-method `LabBackend` interface.
